title: Tilly Turtle's Travelling Bakery | Opposites Story for Kids

music.personality: rolling seaside bakery song with tactile food percussion
music.emotional_arrangement: pizzicato strings and brushed wheel rhythm at dawn; marimba and hand percussion through the deliveries; a brief gentle harmonic pause at the mix-up; brass bell, breadstick taps, wheel brush and full sing-along at the sunset picnic

voices.delivery: bright melodic delivery with acted character choices and a fully sung final refrain; no flat reading

continuity.tilly: one friendly jade-green turtle with warm hazel eyes, honey-amber domed shell patterned with cream spiral scutes, coral baker kerchief and ivory linen apron
continuity.pip: one tiny sandy-brown sandpiper with navy cap and sky-blue delivery satchel
continuity.cart: one coral-and-turquoise painted wooden bakery cart with striped fabric canopy, brass bell and large cream-rimmed wheels
continuity.customers: one silver-grey seal pup in teal scarf, one cream young goat in mustard vest, and two puffin siblings in plum and sea-green scarves
continuity.food_truth: warm soft bun, cool berry bowl, soft crescent roll, crunchy breadsticks, one whole seeded round loaf and exactly two matching semicircular halves
continuity.route: bakery at dawn, warm-to-cool cliff lane, misty pier, lighthouse garden, cove cottage, downhill procession and sheltered sunset beach

scenes.action: Tilly and Pip load the travelling cart at golden dawn, visibly separating warm steaming buns from a cool condensed berry bowl.
lyrics: Morning warms the harbour gold.
Buns are warm; berries cool.
Roll with Tilly, round we go!
scenes.hero: active cart preparation and first warm/cool contrast

scenes.action: The cart rolls from the warm village light toward the cool blue mist of the pier while all food stays secured.
lyrics: Warm sun fades to misty blue.
Warm and cool ride safely through.
Wheel turns; follow to the pier!
scenes.hero: rolling wheel across warm and cool zones

scenes.action: At the pier the seal pup compares a warm soft bun with cool berries and politely chooses the bun.
lyrics: Kiko sees two tasty choices.
Warm soft bun, or berries cool?
Warm and soft for me, please!

scenes.action: At the lighthouse garden Tilly presses a soft roll while Pip taps crunchy breadsticks; the goat chooses crunchy.
lyrics: Marnie meets a texture pair.
Soft roll here; crunchy sticks there.
Crunchy sticks, please, Tilly!
scenes.hero: soft dent versus rigid breadstick texture

scenes.action: At the cove cottage Tilly discovers one whole loaf beside two puffins holding half-shaped plates; Pip checks two half tokens.
lyrics: Two puffins wait by turquoise door.
One whole loaf; two half plates.
Pause and check the shapes.
scenes.hero: one whole circle versus two half plates

scenes.action: The loaf is safely divided off-screen; Tilly places one equal semicircular half on each puffin's plate.
lyrics: One whole becomes two halves.
Equal pieces, one for each.
Two happy halves fit perfectly!
scenes.hero: two equal bread halves with matching crumb faces

scenes.action: The customers carry their exact choices behind Tilly's rolling cart toward a shared sunset picnic.
lyrics: Every neighbour joins the trail.
Bring your choice; share at sunset.
Bell leads everyone downhill!
scenes.hero: connected moving procession with truthful foods

scenes.action: Everyone arranges warm/cool, soft/crunchy and the two separate loaf halves side by side on the beach blanket.
lyrics: Warm, cool; soft, crunchy.
Two halves nearly make one whole.
Opposite partners, side by side!
scenes.hero: all three opposite pairs physically visible

scenes.action: The first full bakery-band finale uses real bell, breadstick-tap, wheel-brush and clap effects while the puffins demonstrate two halves making one whole.
lyrics: Warm or cool; soft or crunchy!
Half plus half makes one whole!
Roll with Tilly, share the treat!
scenes.hero: active ensemble and sung opposites refrain

quality_requirements: Tilly, Pip, the cart, customers, costumes and food shapes retain exact identity across the route.
Every sung opposite is visible for the whole matching phrase and remains physically truthful.
The whole/half mix-up appears only at the cove cottage and is corrected with exactly two equal semicircular halves; no cutting action is shown.
The picnic is set up in scene 8, but the first full ensemble performance is reserved for scene 9.
Real bell, breadstick-tap, wheel-brush and clap effects replace spoken imitation words.
No customer eats during comparison shots; choices are handled cleanly and safely.
The generated artwork contains no text; the deterministic end card appears only after the final scene.
All shared gates in premium-musical-video-set-2026-08-31.json pass before release.
